elements.element: Non-solicit obligation is mutual (binds both parties, not Customer only)
elements.evidence: "This restriction is mutual: neither party shall solicit personnel of the other party"

elements.element: Scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services
elements.evidence: "Section 12.4 is limited to personnel directly involved in the Services"

elements.element: Period measured from the end of that individual's involvement (not from the end of the term)
elements.evidence: "from the end of that individual's involvement in the Services rather than from the end of the term"

elements.element: Carve-out for general advertisements / general recruitment
elements.evidence: "responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment activity not targeted at the other party's personnel"
"who makes an unsolicited approach to a party"
revised 12.4 reads "shall not solicit any Vendor employee" ("hire, or employ" deleted); "neither party is subject to any no-hire obligation"

elements.element: No non-solicit binding Customer at all
elements.evidence: "12.4 Customer shall not solicit any Vendor employee during the term or for 12 months afterward." — a non-solicit still binds Customer

reasons: All six atomic fallback elements are present in operative text: mutuality, scope limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12-month duration, measured from end of involvement, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and express negation of any no-hire duty.
Preferred (no non-solicit on Customer) is not met because a 12-month non-solicit still binds Customer, but the drafter's locked target is the fallback, so this is acceptable and not a deviation.

Edits are confined to § 12.4: the no-hire limbs and the 24-month/"regardless of how the employee applies" language were struck and the shortfalls cured by a single added sentence; § 12.3 and all unrelated terms remain untouched and effective.

Minor drafting nit only (rationale-level, not a deviation): the retained "during the term or for 12 months afterward" in § 12.4 overlaps with the inserted measuring rule, but the insertion expressly supersedes it ("rather than from the end of the term"), so no contradiction or dangling mechanic results.
